task: Lightly copyedit this plain-text folder guide for new volunteers. Retain the useful explanation of why consistent labels help, even though the explanation applies to many projects. Return the passage unchanged if it already communicates the supplied procedure clearly; do not rewrite just to produce visible activity.
input: Label each folder with its project name and the month it was opened. A consistent label helps people tell similar folders apart. Put completed work in the Archive folder so active work stays easy to find.

facts.text: The fictional team's folder labels contain the project name and the month the folder was opened.
Consistent folder labels help this team distinguish similar folders.
The team puts completed work in the Archive folder.
Separating completed work from active work helps this team find active work.

forbidden_additions: An automated archiving feature or deletion schedule.
Additional mandatory folder levels or naming fields.

preserve: The general but useful explanation connecting consistent labels to distinguishing folders.
